content.title: Francesca Fagnani Returns to TV with 'Belve'
content.text: Francesca Fagnani returns to TV on November 19 with the new season of 'Belve'. The journalist and host, one of the most beloved by the audience, became famous for the first question she asks each of her guests to start the provocative interviews that made her famous: 'What beast do you feel like?'. To the same question, she replied: 'A Jack Russell, friendly but if it gets your calf...'. Amendola: 'With the Cesaroni, I bought three houses. The divorce from Francesca Neri was painful. I was addicted to cocaine'. The news of Belve and Giambruno as a guest The journalist was a guest on November 10 at Che Tempo che fa and told Fabio Fazio some of the previews related to the guests of the next season, among which Andrea Giambruno, former partner of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, should appear. 'But is that the last episode, or will there be more?' Fazio asks ironically, with Fagnani responding: 'He is happy to come, but it's not certain, negotiations with Mediaset are still ongoing'. The relationship with the guests and Belve: 'With some, I became friends' The host explained that during the interviews, a sort of seduction relationship is created, which inevitably leads to consolidating or starting an honest relationship with the guests themselves: 'With some, I became friends. With Antonella Clerici, for example. They exert a seduction on me, although not all, including women'. Fagnani then emphasized that the most interesting aspect of her interviews is clearly the shadow areas: 'Much more fascinating than the lights. Firstly because they are more hidden, so bringing them out is fascinating'. The cut interviews Finally, there was talk of the difficulty of making a program like Belve: 'Investigative journalism is a breath of fresh air compared to Belve. The casting is difficult, guests often change their minds, management is very complicated. Initially, it always happened that they asked us for cuts, especially on things that were the news in the end'. An inevitable passage on partner Enrico Mentana: 'After the marathons, Enrico returns fresher than ever, the opposite of what happens after vacations, which destroy him'. Francesca Fagnani, who she is Francesca Fagnani was born on November 25, 1976, in Rome. From a young age, she had a strong passion for journalism, an ambition that led her to pursue high-level studies. Graduated in Literature with a specialization in Dante's Philology, she then continued with a research doctorate, demonstrating a strong inclination for the humanities. Her career in journalism has been marked by determination and tenacity, qualities that have made her one of the most respected figures in the Italian television landscape. Career Francesca Fagnani took her first steps in journalism working for Rai. She was in New York when the Twin Towers collapsed on September 11, 2001, in a terrorist attack, and it seems that was the occasion that started the collaboration. Back in the capital, Fagnani had another important experience, that at 'Annozero', a program by Giovanni Minoli and Michele Santoro. One of Francesca Fagnani's first broadcasts was called 'Il prezzo': there, the journalist interviewed boys serving a prison sentence in juvenile detention for crimes related to organized crime. It is a topic that is still very close to Fagnani's heart, who focused her monologue as co-host of Sanremo 2023 on that subject. Meanwhile, at the time, the journalist was also writing for the newspaper 'la Repubblica'. The success of Belve Her great breakthrough came with the hosting of the program 'Belve', first aired on Nove and then on Rai 2, a format distinguished by incisive and provocative interviews with famous and controversial figures. Thanks to her direct style, she managed to win over the audience and critics, becoming one of the most authoritative voices on Italian television. Her ability to ask uncomfortable questions, without ever being intrusive, has consolidated her status as a courageous and independent journalist. 'Belve came after 20 years of work, no one gave it to me', she said in an interview. Sanremo In February 2023, she took the stage of the Ariston for the first time for an evening alongside Amadeus and Gianni Morandi. The journalist hosted the second evening of the Festival, saying it was 'an honor and a great joy' for her. Love with Enrico Mentana For over 10 years, Francesca Fagnani has been romantically linked to Enrico Mentana, the famous journalist and director of TG La7. Their relationship is characterized by strong privacy. Both prefer to keep their private and public spheres separate. In various interviews, Fagnani has explained that, although very much in love, marriage is not a priority for them: 'For me, marriage is neither a need nor a desire for fulfillment'. She recounted that the first kiss between the two happened in an elevator and that Mentana had to court her for a long time before winning her over. In an interview with Oggi, she said that mutual friends in the mountains brought them together, but it wasn't easy to make her fall: 'He had to court me for a very long time'. But how long? She says at least a year and a half. Because she wasn't sure, because 'there isn't always love at first sight. Some people grow inside you'. The foot photos In their relationship, Fagnani has repeatedly emphasized the importance of maintaining her professional independence, stating: 'I did everything on my own, for better or worse'. Despite the couple's notoriety, both prefer to avoid talking about work at home, thus maintaining a balance between professional life and affections. On the topic of jealousy, she confessed to having spied on her partner's phone in the past 'but he has set up a hundred passwords and eight facial recognitions: I can't access it anymore'. He, on his part, is not jealous: 'I have many more suitors now than before. They contact me even on social media and ask me many times for foot photos. Someone once wrote to me: "Please, can you show your feet on TV for five minutes"'. The missed children Francesca Fagnani does not have children but has declared to have a great relationship with her partner's children. In an interview with Il Messaggero, she commented on the status of a childless woman and the lack of imbalance in not having children: 'No particular reason. It didn't happen to me, I don't miss it, and I think you can be happy even without children'. Marriage? 'They asked me a couple of times, but I ran away. I don't believe in love forever'. The death of her mother 'I felt a very strong love for my mother, when I lost her, seven years ago' - she said in 2022 - 'it was a slap, for a long time I felt a sort of void. What I felt for my mother was overwhelming, irrecoverable love. No one can care for me and love me like a mother'. © ALL RIGHTS RESERVED This article is automatically translated
